annotations.text:
PICK A DIRECTION FOR THE PALETTE

Three ways the summoned window could work. All three use the dashboard's exact tokens - #0A0B10 ground, the rgba(255,255,255,0.035) wash, 20px surfaces, 100px pills, Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono - so the choice is about behaviour, not styling.

A is on the top row in both its states; B and C are below.

A - SPOTLIGHT
One column, one input, nothing else. Opens fastest to read, stays honest to "type and go", and the same window works at any size. Costs: you must press Tab to see or change anything about an entry.

B - CONSOLE
A permanent right pane showing whatever is highlighted, so limits and toggles are one keystroke away without leaving the palette. Costs: a much wider window, and more to read every time you summon it for a plain launch.

C - HEADS-UP
Drops from the top of the screen and always shows how the day is going. Answers "how am I doing" with no typing. Costs: the ambient half is dead weight when you only want to launch something, and a short bar leaves little room for results.

EVERYTHING THE CURRENT APP DOES, ACCOUNTED FOR

These carry direction A's language through the rest of the product. Nothing from today's app was dropped: display name, executable path, hotkey capture and clear, don't-pass-through, daily limit with force close and its PIN-locked state, launch arguments, startup delay, auto-start, per-entry stats, reordering, the scanner, and every setting including the startup-conflict banner and rollback.

The Statistics tab is the one deliberate removal - it only ever held a button to the browser.

STILL OPEN

Where the tray menu's Extend time dialog lives - I have assumed it becomes a palette command rather than its own window, but it has to work when a browser is restricted, so it may deserve to stay separate.

The OSD and the auto-launch progress popup are unchanged in this pass.
